items_missed: Never asked for or used the customer's name — she gave it in her first sentence ('my name is Saila') and he used 'ma'am' the whole call instead
No 'How are you today?', no agenda statement, no 'sound good?' confirmation
Never confirmed or even discussed the move date — the customer opened by saying she called to 'lock in the dates' and no date was ever named
Never stated the hourly rate — quoted only totals ($1,526 at 7 hours), so the customer has no per-hour number to compare against the other movers she said she'd been quoting
No 'pricing is super simple' framing, no list of what's included, no disassembly/reassembly mention (she has two standing desks and two bed frames)
No No Worries Damage Coverage — she has a glass dining table and an unboxed 75-inch TV going down from a 21st floor, and the $2,000 coverage never came up
No Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no 'no hidden fees' pitch
Clock section almost entirely skipped — no on-site start, no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute increments (only credit was the sense-check)
Never stated number of movers or trucks behind the 5.75-7 hour estimate

Save Your Ass speech skipped entirely — no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip. This was the obvious answer to her seven-hour objection and he never reached for it
No booking attempt at all — the customer called specifically to book, he raised the estimate, and then handed her off to 'chat it over with your husband' without asking for the schedule
No deposit never mentioned — the strongest available objection-handler on a price-shock call and it was left on the table
No BOLDED email detail list, no 'reply with any corrections', no business hours
top_strength: Genuinely excellent estimate integrity — he caught that the prior rep's 5.75-hour quote was thin for a 21st-floor load-up, walked her through why (square footage normal, box count low, but the high-rise load adds time), gave a real 5.75-to-7-hour range, and framed it honestly: he'd rather she get sticker shock before the move than after. He also handled the TV-without-a-box question well (TV bag up to 55 inches, pad wrap and shrink above that, no extra charge) and got a natural laugh out of the mattress exchange.
coaching_note: Dustin did the hard, honest thing on the estimate and then dropped the sale. When you raise a number on a customer, you have to give them something back in the same breath: the Save Your Ass prep speech (her 15 boxes and pre-booked service elevator both pull time down), No Worries coverage for the glass table and 75-inch TV, and no deposit required so booking costs her nothing while she talks to her husband. He turned a ready-to-book customer into a maybe.
phone_presence_notes: Warm, patient, and genuinely honest — the mattress joke, repeated 'if that makes sense' checks, and empathy on her seven-hour concern kept the customer comfortable even while he was delivering bad news, though he never once used her name.
